text_devanagari: अ॒ना॒गसं॒ ब्रह्म॑णा त्वा कृणोमि शि॒वे ते॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी उ॒भे स्ता॑म् ॥ ९ ॥
notes: Line starts with a wide blank/indent at the left of the first segment; text begins mid-way. Band separation was clean and decisive: line pitch ~170 px, the middle line's headline occupies y=103-117, its anudatta bars sit in y=206-224, and the line above's bars sit in y=38-54, so no bar was ambiguous between lines. 7 anudatta (a, na, sam, shi, te, thi, u) and 3 svarita (over hma of brahmana, over va of dyavaprithivi, over sta of stam). Two apparent 'bars' in the anudatta band were rejected as vowel signs, not accents: the descending curl of the vocalic-r matra under कृ (seg1 x=1200-1231) and under पृ (seg2 x=629-663) - both are hooks, not straight bars, and each is the tail of its own aksara. The mark above सं (seg1 x=644-663) is the anusvara dot, not a svarita: it is roundish and wide, unlike the narrow straight strokes (width ~9-11 px) confirmed as svarita. Curved wide shapes above the headline over णो, मि, थि, वी, भे, वे, ते and शि were all read as i/o/e/ii matras, not accents. Accent placement in this fount is consistently centred on the aksara's vertical stem, which is what was used to assign each bar to an aksara. The second aksara of ब्रह्मणा is a ligature read as ह्म with moderate confidence (fount is unfamiliar); the reading of the aksara body, not the accent, is the softer part. The closing numeral is read as ९ (loop plus descending tail), not १.
